preamble: Vocalization of a nasal consonant to the vowel [i]. In Spokane (Interior Salish), the process known as nasal shift turns a nasal immediately followed by a coronal fricative (/s/, /š/, also /h/) into [i] when syllabification requires a nucleus, or into the glide [j] otherwise. It most often affects the final /n/ of a root or suffix before /s/, including /n/ left next to /s/ after the /t/ of -n-t-əs is dropped, and also applies to /m/. It is a morphophonemic rule rather than automatic allophony: it is not fully general, is restricted to the prefixal and suffixal domains (not root-internal), and competes with nasal deletion and fricative hardening in the same environment.

examples.note: The root-final /n/ before the possessive suffix -s surfaces as syllabic [i].
The /n/ of the proclitic čn becomes [i] before /s/ within the prefixal domain; compare hin-s-√mʔem > hismʔém 'she is my woman', where the /n/ deletes instead.
